name: Neuramis

card.summary: A Korean hyaluronic acid filler range from Medytox used to smooth lines and add volume to lips, cheeks and the mid-face.
card.aka: Medytox HA filler; Neuramis Deep, Volume, Light
card.note: Injected by clinicians; availability varies by country and the line is not FDA-approved in the US.[1]

quick.overview:
Neuramis is a line of cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers made by South Korean company Medytox. Variants are designed for different depths, from superficial lines to nasolabial folds, lips and volume in areas such as the cheeks and chin.[1]

For appearance, HA fillers add volume and smooth folds, which can restore mid-face fullness or refine contour. Randomized trials in Korea compared Neuramis products with Restylane, Perlane and Juvederm Voluma and reported similar results.[2][3][4][5]
quick.how: A trained clinician injects the gel, and many variants include lidocaine for comfort.[4] Results are described as lasting months rather than permanently; in one mid-face study about 73 to 74 percent of subjects still responded at 104 weeks.[3] Hyaluronidase can dissolve HA fillers.[6]
quick.risks: Reported effects of HA fillers include swelling, bruising, redness and in rare cases vascular occlusion or granulomas.[6] In a network meta-analysis of cheek fillers, Giselleligne showed fewer adverse events than Neuramis Lidocaine, while efficacy scores did not differ significantly.[7] Neuramis has not received US FDA approval.[1]

lead: Neuramis is a range of cross-linked hyaluronic acid dermal fillers manufactured by Medytox, a South Korean biopharmaceutical company. Its variants include Light (superficial wrinkles and skin hydration), standard and Deep (medium to deep wrinkles, nasolabial folds, lips) and Volume (cheeks, chin and contouring), many with lidocaine for comfort.[1]

People use HA fillers to soften folds, add lip fullness and restore or build mid-face volume. Hyaluronic acid binds water and swells into a gel, and the effect of fillers generally lasts about 6 to 12 months.[6]

Published research on Neuramis consists mostly of Korean randomized, split-face comparisons. A 2015 phase III trial found Neuramis Deep non-inferior to Restylane for nasolabial folds,[5] a 2016 trial found Neuramis Deep Lidocaine scored somewhat better than Perlane-L on wrinkle and global improvement scales at 24 weeks,[4] and a mid-face trial found Neuramis Volume Lidocaine non-inferior to Juvederm Voluma.[2]

chain: Clinician injects HA gel into folds, lips or cheeks
Gel binds water and adds volume
Smoother folds and fuller mid-face for months
angle.text: Neuramis fillers add volume where the face has lost or lacks it. Different variants are formulated for fine lines, nasolabial folds, lips and cheeks.

infobox: Light, standard, Deep, Volume, with lidocaine options[1]

paras: Neuramis variants target different depths: lighter products for fine lines and hydration, mid-depth products for wrinkles and lips, and Volume for cheek and chin contouring.[1] Cosmetic clinics offering Korean aesthetic procedures commonly use such fillers for mid-face restoration and nasolabial folds.

In a split-face trial of 88 Korean adults with age-related mid-face volume deficit, Neuramis Volume Lidocaine and Juvederm Voluma with Lidocaine each produced a 96.39% response rate at 24 weeks, meeting non-inferiority.[2] A 2-year extension followed 69 participants: responder rates were 73.91% for Neuramis and 72.46% for Juvederm at week 104, with no serious adverse events.[3]

For nasolabial folds, a 67-person phase III trial found Neuramis Deep not inferior to Restylane with no significant difference in safety.[5] A 58-patient trial found Wrinkle Severity Rating Scale improvement of 1.64 for Neuramis Deep Lidocaine versus 1.45 for Perlane-L at week 24.[4]

HA fillers can cause redness, itching, bruising, nerve or microvessel injury and, in rare cases, vascular occlusion or granulomatous reactions.[6] A 2024 network meta-analysis of six randomized trials (579 patients) reported Giselleligne had fewer adverse events than VYC-20, ART-Filler and Neuramis Lidocaine, with no significant GAIS differences among fillers.[7]
In a mini-pig study comparing 14 HA fillers, Neuramis products tended to show lower inflammatory cell infiltration than Juvederm and Restylane products.[8]

Neuramis is registered in South Korea and Europe, and is not FDA-approved in the United States.[1] It is one of several Korean HA filler brands in a market that also includes Restylane, Juvederm and Belotero.

Randomized, intraindividual trials compared Neuramis with Restylane or Perlane for nasolabial folds and with Juvederm Voluma for mid-face volume, finding non-inferiority or small advantages at 24 weeks and durable results up to 104 weeks.[2][3][4][5] A network meta-analysis of cheek fillers found no significant difference in aesthetic improvement scores between fillers.[7]
